Install bun on Omarchy

Bun is an all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit: a fast runtime (built in Rust/Zig on JavaScriptCore rather than V8) meant as a drop-in alternative to Node.js, plus a built-in package manager, bundler, and test runner in a single executable. The goal is to collapse a typical JS project's separate tools into one fast binary, cutting install and startup times compared to a traditional Node/npm/webpack/Jest stack.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add bun-bin
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 1.4.3-1:
    pacman -Qi bun-bin

Open and use bun

bun has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql bun-bin | grep /usr/bin/

bun requirements and compatibility

  • Linux kernel 5.6+ recommended (5.1 minimum)

Pricing and license

Free and open source (MIT licensed, open source). License: MIT.

Frequently asked questions

How do I install bun on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add bun-bin. The download is 41 MB and it takes 89 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is bun free?

Free and open source (MIT licensed, open source). The package is licensed MIT.

How do I uninstall bun?

Run omarchy pkg drop bun-bin. It removes the package from your system.

What does bun depend on?

bun declares no dependencies in the Omarchy package database.

Is bun a desktop app?

No. bun has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is bun in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as bun-bin (version 1.4.3-1) in the official Omarchy package repository. Bun makes it. Project site: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun.
